decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1% to 1.25%. The vote was 9-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising moderately so far this year.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in May indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity h…”

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have moderated but have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined.”

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment have continued to expand.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has picked up in recent months, and business fixed investment has continued to expand.”

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On a 12-month basis, inflation has declined recently and, like the measure excluding food and energy prices, is running somewhat below 2 percent.”

changes.quote: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1 to 1-1/4…”

changes.quote: For the time being, the Committee is maintaining its existing policy of reinvesting principal payments from its holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities in agency mortgage-backed securities and of rolling over maturing Treasury securities at auction.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting some further strengthening in labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.
Job gains have been solid, on average, since the beginning of the year, and the unemployment rate has declined.
On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and the measure excluding food and energy prices have declined and are running below 2 percent.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.54% APR costs about $52.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.29% and moved -4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.03% would fall by about $6.92 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.3%, and employers added an average of 204k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.6% over the past year (June 2017); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -4 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.03%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.09% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is balanced. The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 89%, cut 0%, hike 11%.
